text.p: These are the highlights of the main Sao Paulo and Rio de Janeiro newspapers this morning.
GAZETA MERCANTIL
-- BRAZIL IS NOT SELLING ABROAD KEY TECHNOLOGICAL PRODUCTS

Brazil does not export any of the products which are showing the most global growth. Between 1985 and 1995, world sales of micro-circuit electronics increased on average 73.24 percent per year while those of soybeans, an important part of Brazilian exports, grew only 2.8 percent on average.
-- WORLD BANK PROPOSES SOLUTIONS FOR UNEMPLOYMENT
The World Bank believes Brazil should deregulate the workplace, update laws from the 1950s and 1960s and reduce costs for employers in order to reduce Brazilian unemployment
-- GEORGE SOROS IS INVESTING HEAVILY IN ARGENTINE LAND
George Soros is investing heavily in Argentine agricultural land and already owns 338,100 hectares of land being used for grain production, cattle-rearing and other products.
FOLHA DE SAO PAULO
-- SAO PAULO CITY COUNCIL HAS DELAYED PAYMENT OF JUDICIAL DEBTS
Sao Paulo city council is late in paying at least 90 million reais in judicial debts. In March, Paulo Maluf said that there was no delay in payments.
-- SAO PAULO MILITARY POLICE HOSPITAL SEES NEW DRUG CASE EVERY DAY

The Sao Paulo military police hospital receives a new case of drug addiction every day. According to statistics, the percentage of drug addicts among new recruits has grown 10 times in the last 10 years.
O GLOBO
-- PRESIDENT CARDOSO TO CREATE HUMAN RIGHTS SECRETARIAT
President Fernando Henrique Cardoso will sign an act today creating a National Human Rights Secretariat attached to the Justice Ministry.
-- PRIVATISATION OF B BAND COULD REDUCE RATES BY 30 PERCENT

Telecommunications Minister Sergio Motta believes the eventual winners of a tender for B Band cellular telephone concessions should propose rates at least 30 percent lower than those currently charged by Telebras
-- SUPREME TRIBUNAL DEFENDS SALARY ADJUSTMENT FOR CIVIL SERVANTS

A minister from the Supreme Federal Tribunal (STF) said the continued failure of the Administration Ministry to adjust public workers' salaries could result in the government being accused of an act against the constitution.
-- Reuters has not verified the stories and cannot vouch for their accuracy.
((-- Caroline Bulloch, Rio de Janeiro newsroom, 5521 5074151))
